narration.transcript: Want the look of old timber beams without the weight? Meet Heritage Timber from Ekena Millwork. Each beam is molded in one piece from real, weathered timber. Pick from six textures, Mina, salvaged timber, rustic sawn, resawn rip, reclaimed axe cut, and sanded smooth. Then a hand-stained finish, sandstone, kona brown, vanilla chai, warm caramel, natural white oak, smoky brown, or primed ready to paint. Eight sizes from three and a half inches square to nine and a half by 11 and a half in lengths from four to 24 feet. They're hollow, so they slide over a wood block on your ceiling and can hide wiring. And they ship fast, stained beams in three to five business days, primed in about one to three. Order a sample and see it in your own light.

findings.what: In the 16:9 cut the room photo is cropped to the lower room: the ceiling beams are out of frame (only two dark corners show at the very top) while the narration says 'the look of old timber beams' and the card says 'The timber look.' The opening 4 s show no beam. The 9:16 cut of the same photo shows the beams.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, timeline key 'hook': re-anchor the 16:9 crop/Ken-Burns of research/product-images/heritage__angles__BMSTKB-09.jpg to the top of the photo (vaulted ceiling and beams in frame), or use a landscape room photo where the beams sit in the 16:9 frame; move the card down/left so it stays off the beams.

findings.what: In the 9:16 cut the texture title 'Reclaimed Axed Cut' runs off the right edge and reads 'Reclaimed Axed Cu' for the whole slide.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, timeline key 'textures' (tex_5): in the 9:16 layout shrink-to-fit the texture name to the safe width (or wrap to two lines) instead of using the fixed 16:9 font size.

findings.what: At every finish change the outgoing and incoming names (and their eyebrows) are drawn on top of each other at full strength for about 13 frames: f1523-1535, 1595-1607 ('Vanilla Chai' over 'Kona Brown'), 1667-1680 ('Vanilla Chai'/'Warm Caramel'), 1739-1751, 1831-1843 and 1920-1932 ('Primed' over 'Smokey Brown', eyebrow 'READY TO PAINT' over 'HAND-STAINED'). The overprint lands right as each name is spoken. Same in both cuts.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, timeline key 'finishes' (fin_2...fin_7 name swap): fade/slide the old name out before the new one comes in (or offset them vertically with a mask) so the two labels never share the same pixels; same for the eyebrow line.

findings.source: research/beam-lines-facts.md, 'Wording to be careful with: Heritage lengths'
findings.what: Card 'Molded in one piece' and narration 'Each beam is molded in one piece', while the sizes scene offers lengths to 24 ft. The README says 16, 20 and 24 ft ship as one long item by freight and warns not to claim one-piece moulding over 12 ft without checking with the plant. H18 is about corner seams, not length.
findings.fix: build/script-v1.json#reveal: say what H18 supports ('Each beam is molded as one piece, with no corner seams' framed as the U-shape), or get the plant to confirm one-piece over 12 ft. Brody to decide.

findings.what: In 9:16 the '11½' height callout beside the 9½×11½ outline is cut off by the right edge (only '11' and part of the fraction show). The '9½×11½' label below still reads.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, timeline key 'sizes' (sizes_big): in the 9:16 layout pull the second row in from the right edge, or place the height callout inside the frame (left of the outline).

findings.what: In 9:16 the burned-in caption 'and can hide wiring.' sits on the bottom of the U-beam diagram, covering the beam's bottom wall right where the wiring is being drawn.
